prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your situation (individual vs employer, ACA marketplace vs private plan, Medicare, narrow-network needs, budget, etc.). A few quick questions will let me give specific broker names and a short list to contact:

- Are you in Kansas City, Missouri or Kansas City, Kansas? (Zip code helps.)
- Is this for individual/family coverage, a small business group plan, or Medicare/Medicare Advantage/Medigap?
- Are you shopping during open enrollment or a special enrollment period?
- Any must-have doctors, hospitals, medications, or budget limits?

While you answer, here are practical tips and resources so you can quickly find a good broker and vet them:

How to find brokers and what to check
- Use official search tools: healthcare.gov’s “Find Local Help,” Missouri Division of Finance & Insurance or Kansas Insurance Department license lookups, or local NAHU/Independent Agents directories. Those show licensed agents/brokers in your area.
- Verify licensing: ask for their license number and confirm it on your state’s insurance department website.
- Look for specialization: brokers often focus on ACA/open-market plans, employer group benefits, or Medicare. Choose one with the right focus.
- Ask how they’re paid: most brokers are paid by insurers (no direct fee), but confirm if they charge you any broker fee.
- Ask for references or client reviews and check Google/Yelp/Angie’s List.
- Ask whether they represent multiple carriers (independent broker) or just one company (captive agent). Independent brokers can typically show more options.
- Ask sample questions: “Which carriers do you work with?”, “Can you show cost estimates including premiums, deductibles, co-pays, and out-of-pocket max?”, “How will you help if a claim is denied?”, “Do you help with enrollment and ongoing support?”
- Red flags: pressure to sign immediately, refusal to disclose carriers or compensation, unwillingness to provide references.

Local resources (start here)
- healthcare.gov — “Find Local Help” tool for in-person or virtual assisters and brokers.
- Missouri Division of Insurance license lookup and consumer pages.
- Kansas Insurance Department license lookup and consumer pages.
- National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) — find local brokers and chapters.
- Independent Insurance Agents associations for Missouri/Kansas.

If you want, give your zip code and the type of coverage (individual/family, small business, Medicare), and I’ll pull together a short, current list of nearby, well-reviewed independent brokers and what each specializes in.
